title: Platform systems & services 1 HowTos, Dashboards, Runbooks, Retrospective, and Roadmap (Team Wiki) - Addendum
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Purpose:
This addendum captures clarifications and small updates to the canonical team wiki for platform systems & services (HowTos, Dashboards, Runbooks, Retrospective, and Roadmap). It is intended as a lightweight update to correct examples, add a few quick mitigations, and call out immediate action items identified in the Feb 2026 game day.

Summary of changes:
- Clarified alert thresholds for p95-based autoscaling (see Alerting standards).
- Added manual mitigation: router graceful-shutdown command and safe drain steps.
- Updated roadmap milestone dates and delivery owners for Q2 initiatives.

Quick reference (new mitigations):
- Router graceful drain (use when upgrading router replicas to avoid request drops):
  1) Mark pod as draining via admin API: curl -X POST $ROUTER_ADMIN/api/v1/pod/drain -d '{"pod":"inference-router-abc123"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  2) Wait for in-flight requests to drain (monitor request_inflight gauge).
  3) Once inflight==0, scale down or restart pod.
- Emergency route blacklist (stop noisey client causing overload):
  curl -X POST $ROUTER_ADMIN/api/v1/clients/blacklist -d '{"client_id":"<id>","duration_seconds":3600}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Alerting standards clarification:
- Autoscaler trigger should prioritize p95 latency when available. Adjust HPA/ClusterAutoscaler triggers to include a p95 metric derived from Prometheus instead of CPU alone for inference-router and model-scheduler. Example HPA metric snippet (conceptual): metric: prometheus/p95_request_latency{job="inference-router"} targetValue: 200ms
- When switching to p95-based autoscaling, keep a CPU-based fallback for lower-traffic windows.

Runbook clarifications:
- High request queueing runbook: add step to verify router drain state and evictions on the queue backend.
- KV cache contamination: recommended immediate mitigation now includes a temporary global TTL parity mode (force uniform TTL across keys) when contamination affects many prefixes.

Roadmap updates (owners & dates):
- 2026-Q2 (owner: Diego Morales): Centralize dashboard templates into grafana.playbooks (deliverable: 12 canonical dashboards). Target completion: 2026-05-15.
- 2026-Q2 (owner: Priya Kapoor): Implement alert dedup fingerprinting. Target completion: 2026-06-01.
- 2026-Q3 (owner: Jordan Lee): Autoscaler improvements (p95-driven autoscaling). Target start: 2026-07-01.

Action items from Feb 2026 game day:
- (Diego) Create Grafana template PR for inference-router and kv-cache-service dashboards. Due: 2026-03-15.
- (Priya) Implement simple alert fingerprinting rule in PD for platform services to reduce duplicate pages. Due: 2026-03-22.
- (Samir) Add router drain check to the high-queueing runbook and add an automated reminder in playbook-runner. Due: 2026-03-10.

Doc housekeeping:
- If you edit a runbook, update the Last updated date in the runbook and add a short changelog entry.
- Stale runbooks (no updates in >12 months) will be reviewed in Q3 cleanup; mark runbooks with 'review_needed' label if they should be preserved.

Links and references:
- Grafana dashboards folder: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/dashboards/eng-platform
- Router admin API docs: /confluence/eng-platform/inference-router-admin-api
- Platform runbooks repo: git@github.com:redwood/platform-runbooks.git (use branch platform-addendum-2026-q2 for PRs)

Revision history:
- 2026-03-02: Addendum published (Ava Thompson).
- 2026-02-10: Original canonical wiki created (Ava Thompson).

Notes:
- This document is an addendum and should be merged into the canonical team wiki during the next scheduled update. For urgent changes, open a PR in the platform-runbooks repo and notify platform-runbooks@redwood.com.
